documents: It states a limit on an effect rather than a value, so nothing in the address records answers it. What would: the audible contrast the archive already measures, run on these addresses, which would show which of them a reader can hear and which they cannot.

It states what one message does to a table, which is a reset by another name and is the shape of thing the archive's reset probe measures. Nothing has put a drum set change to this unit and read these addresses back, so what the document states here stands beside no measurement at all.

The document states elsewhere on this page that selecting an insertion effect type sets that effect's parameters as a group. The initial value in this row is therefore what selecting a type leaves here, not what the unit powers up holding -- and the archive's own effect map records every one of the sixty-five types this unit accepted loading 40 into this address, which is the value stated.
The document states no single initial value for this address. It states one for the SC-8850, SC-88Pro and SC-88 maps, and another for the SC-55 map that depends on whether the part is the drum part.
The document states no single initial value for this address: it depends on the part number.

The note is printed under the drum setup table and names that table's parameters, so it is taken to reach every row of it.

The note names the two parameters, and the two rows carrying those names are the whole of what it reaches. It is about the pair rather than about either of them, which is why it is here rather than restated twice as a qualification.

The write probe writes one address at a time and reads it back, so it would find both of these accepting a value and say nothing about what happens when both hold one. What would answer it is an audible comparison with each set alone and with both set together.
